reasoning: Set B is the stronger set because it reaches the point where building can start and Set A does not. Both sets have careful, look-ahead-aware designs for all four stages: per-window PCA, Marchenko–Pastur denoising, shrinkage and denoised covariance, min-variance, risk parity and HRP with known-answer tests, Holm-corrected null tests and purged splits. A's research and learn pipelines and their golden cases are excellent. But A has no milestones, no tasks/plan.md, no todo.md, no CONSTRAINTS.md, no AGENTS.md and no context packets. Its probes were never run (every verdict is '—'). A builder therefore cannot tell what to build first. A also has a few consistency slips: a wrong cross-reference to 'PL-14's open_loader' (PL-14 is a server pipeline), and the roadmap's S2 skills leave out null-hypothesis-testing even though COV-03 requires it. B has a 7-milestone roadmap with S1 split along dependency lines. M1 is a vertical walking skeleton across eqdata, server and web, with one Phase 0 interface task that freezes all three package boundaries, a clean dependency graph, and 35 task packets that carry the frozen types, the golden cases and checkable acceptance. B uses the user's ten delisted names throughout, routes data-analysis and null-hypothesis-testing to S2 and later, and puts frontend-design on the viz-app tasks. B's weaknesses: a very dense architecture overview, some stale 'used by study and features' wording left over after forecast and agents were added, contract samples marked 'not written yet' in the packets, a very large interface task, and a probe that ran against a localhost endpoint and failed.
